Escutei muito bem de Iconoclast pelos anos, tanto que tenho ele desde 2018, mas depois de jogar fiquei meio confuso.

O jogo primeiramente tem uma estética linda: a ambientação, a movimentação, o character design, os sound effects, tudo é muito imersivo e cativante, é um jogo que encaixa total com o estilo pixel art

O combate é simples mas até que divertido na medida do possível, você tem uma Chave Inglesa para bater nos inimigos e algumas armas com mira semi automatica. E por mais que seja bacana matar monstros nas primeiras horas, você começa a ignora-los pois além de não representar perigo ou desafio, o resto do jogo vai cansando

O maior problema de Iconoclast é o level design e quebra cabeças, a maneira mais fácil de descrever é "Pro desenvolvedor tudo isso faz sentido porque foi ele quem fez, agora para alguém que está jogando não é, porque o player não está dentro da cabeça do dev". O jogo, quando tenta ser mais simples, é um bom passatempo porque ele não exige muito de você, a plataforma é fácil, inimigos não são ameaça e os chefes até que são divertidos tirando algumas exceções. Mas na maior parte do game, os mapas são grandes e fechados, fazendo você ficar correndo em círculos por muito tempo até que finalmente você encontra a sala especifica pra ativar o trigger pra progredir na história, para então ficar procurando onde é a próxima sala pra ativar o próximo trigger.

O level design foi feito para você perder tempo, tanto que, os monstros voltam quando você salva o jogo, fazendo a exploração ser mais estressante do que interessante, sem falar que eles não dão nenhuma recompensa quando são mortos.

Em outros momentos do jogo, não é uma sala especifica que você tem que encontrar, mas sim uma parede invisível sem nenhuma sinalização obvia que você só acabou descobrindo porque ficou minutos rondando o mapa tocando em tudo, no desespero de ter algo que o faça progredir, isso quando você não segue um percurso inteiro realizando quebra cabeças para no final descobrir que você não devia estar naquela saia ainda, fazendo você voltar tudo e então, quando for o momento certo, voltar para essa sala realizando os quebra cabeça novamente.

Um dos maiores problemas do jogo são os quebra cabeças, principalmente por envolverem uma lança granada onde a bomba voa com física, há momentos que você sabe que você tem que atirar em um lugar, mas por algum motivo a bomba não entra, ou ela rola demais e não entra onde deveria, ou ela quica e erra, fazendo você se perguntar se está no local certo ou pensando "Talvez vai ter algum item pra fazer esse puzzle e to perdendo tempo?", mas não, você está no local certo, e está fazendo a coisa certa, mas o jogo tem que "deixar" você acertar o puzzle.

Vários puzzles são muito fora da caixa, como se para o criador fosse obvio o que você tem que fazer porque foi ele quem criou, mas para qualquer pessoa é muito além do "Pensar fora da caixa", a maioria dos quebra cabeças depois de finalmente resolvidos fazem você girar os olhos ao invés de ter sensação de sucesso, algo como "É sério que era ISSO que ele queria??", as vezes tendo que descobrir novas mecânicas que jogo nunca tentou te mostrar em outra hora passada, e que, nunca mais usa novamente.

Ficar preso correndo em círculos pelo mapa porque você não sabe se um quebra cabeça tem que ser feito por um item novo que você não tem ainda ou porque "você não tentou o suficiente", ou porque talvez você deixou passar uma parede invisível ou um buraco ou duto no chão atravessável, faz a experiência do jogo ser absurdamente frustrante, afetando seriamente a história.

Por mais que a história e personagens sejam interessantes (E boa, por sinal), ter que passar uma hora de stress para cada cutscene faz você não estar na vibe para apreciar ela. É como se você estivesse vendo um bom filme, mas a cada 10 minutos você tivesse que fazer uma pausa de 30 minutos raspando as unhas na parede

Se você remover as partes que você está perdido, as horas do jogo caem pela metade

Iconoclast tem ideias bacanas, mas a maior parte do jogo não foi bem pensado

Unfortunately I bounced away hard from this game. And I really don’t know why. Everything — and I mean everything — is more than average from your standard, 2D platformer slop that floods Steam right now. The controls are tight and responsive, the graphics are gorgeous, the story is intriguing and well written… And yet, something fell off.  

Okay, let’s start from the beginning, shall we? First of all, if you are looking for a full fledged metroidvania, you will experience a little let down. Iconoclast is very, very lite in this department. Look at abilities our heroine can unlock — through story progression you can find two upgrades for your gun and two upgrades for your wrench… and nothing more. No dash, no glide, no wall jump, no different weapon type. Nothing, Zero, zip, nada. In some cases you can combine your abilities — like electrifying your grenades by using your wrench — but this is used mostly to solve puzzles and unlocking the chests rather than for actual combat. The only way you can develop your character is by equipping tweaks — little technical do-dats that can slightly change behaviour of our heroine or her weapon; for example, you can run a little faster, spin your wrench longer or extend her breath under water. They are not crucial to progression and their impact on gameplay is so insignificant, that you can ignore them completely and still win the game. More to this — they can brake. If you get hit even one time, they will be unusable until you kill enough enemies or use meditation tweak. The most important one — double jump — can only be obtained after defeating a hidden boss, with which you gain access to around ¾ of the game. Yeah, you read it correctly — one of the most crucial mechanics in other platformer games here is a side content, which can break when you get hit. Another important tweak is immunity to damage — it breaks without you losing health — and only because of challenge mode, where you die from one hit.

No better is with levels. They all are very straightforward, limited with exploration. You basically travel from one big set piece and puzzle through corridors and rooms only from time to time occupied by enemies. What is more important, the exploration is pointless, since your only reward is finding a chest that contains upgrade materials for tweaks. They are especially pointless in NG+, if you collected all the tweaks in normal playthrough. 

All of the above is subjective. You can still enjoy Iconoclast without metroidvania mechanics. Hell, I didn’t mind this very casual approach to genre, well aside all those hooplas I was forced to endure to get double jump. No, I have different problem, that can be described in one word:

Gimmicks.

This game is full of them. It focuses more on puzzles than exploration and combat. It’s room after room of environmental puzzles, puzzles where you need your tools, timed puzzles and jumping puzzles. Hell, even enemies and big chunks of bosses — not all, mind you — are built around gimmicks. There are monsters that can only be damaged in specific ways, using specific tools, or even some of them cannot be damaged at all, only avoided entirely. No better is with some bosses — it’s like a mechanical dance, where your moves are calculated, so just wait until a window of opportunity for dealing some damage appears. The only redeeming quality of this is that they all are unique — you cannot just spam bullets and avoid their attack, because all of them have different quirks and ideas built into fight. One of the bosses is this giant reactor that you need to take down with the help of your companion, another is a centipede-like train that you fight in a big rounded area… The creativity of this encounter shines at every step, even if sometimes they are hit or miss, like with Mother boss fight; avoid her 4 or 5 attacks just to have one opportunity to strike and do some damage. Repeat through 3 phases. Riveting gameplay. 

But there is another, big shade to all of this. Because of all of these puzzles and gimmicks thrown constantly at you, at some point the game just becomes a chore. And I know, it’s built on a premise that our main heroine is a mechanic, so we mostly fix things, but good God, I just want some time to shoot things, especially after I spend 15 minutes on one puzzle room, just to travel two empty screen forward just for ANOTHER puzzle room. This is especially frustrating if you take into consideration that this game doesn't have a checkpoint system, only manual saves and autosaves before bosses, so if you waste time on a puzzle, and then go and die in the next room, you need to do the entire puzzle AGAIN. At some point I just gave up and started save-scumming — after  solving the puzzle I just run back to the save station to store my progress. Over, and over again.  

Well, maybe something about the story… Don’t get fooled by bright, colorful graphics, cute looking characters and joyful music. After a speedy introduction that sets false expectations of quirky action oriented, lighthearted story, the game suddenly has a very dark turn into more serious territory. People dying here horrible deaths, losing families, limbs, LITERALLY MELTING before our eyes. The Game does not shy to ask profound questions about purpose, destiny, faith or religion — and without this  condescending, patronizing tone of “religion le bad and thats it”. It is a heavy story-oriented experience, albeit not without flaws. This game makes the mistake of not establishing proper world building at the beginning, nor spending some time on plot to breath, grow and focus on details and nuances, so for some time you are really confused about what is going on here. Plus you're introduced to many characters at once, and several of them are just nothing but fillers, that you really feel like on some wild rolecoster, constantly pushed forward without understanding who all of those people are and what they are doing.  

Finally, something about challenge mode. When I die, the devil will probably drag me to hell and torture me for eternity by forcing me play ♥♥♥♥ like this. ONE HIT GAMEPLAY. You die from one hit. Good luck beating the entire game like that. Yes, you can use immunity to do damage tweak, stack them up to three times, so you can have three hits before dying, BUT! There are sections in this game where you play different characters. And tweaks DO NOT TRANSFER TO THEM. All Mina’s sections were pure nightmares. No better with some bosses. It took me more than 100 times (yes, ONE HUNDRED) to finally beat the second boss fight with Agent Black. Play this mode only if you really want achievement or love to suffer.

Now. It's over. Go home or something.

アクションゲームとしては非常に面白い作品。
ボスで何度も死んでやり直すタイプのゲームではなく、難易度は高くない。
そしてステージ数とパズルのバリエーションが多く、さまざまなギミックを解いていくのはとても楽しかった。
特にボス戦は、操作テクニックよりも「どうすれば倒せるか」のギミックを解かないと勝てないタイプで、アクションよりもパズル性のほうが高い作品だと感じる。
グラフィックについても見た通り、こだわりというか執念を感じる美グラ。


一方でストーリーとキャラクターは壊滅的に合わなかった。
ストーリーは、ポップなキャラのイメージからは遠いキリスト教終末的世界観ベースにあり、会話が難解（そうに見えるが、それっぽいワードが混ざるだけで、あまり奥深さも感じられなかった）。

そしてキャラクターはほぼ全員、とても動物的で独りよがりなタイプばかり。
基本的に相手の話を真正面から返さないので対話が成立しないし、自分のしたいことしかしない、人の話を力で遮って勝手に突っ走る、かと思えば俺ってこんな辛い過去なんだぜ自慢ばかりで、全く共感できなかった。

本作の主人公はいわゆる「一言も話さない系」女子で、こういうキャラの場合、プレイヤーが主人公に感情移入する余地を残すという演出でもあり、まあ有る有るではある
しかし本作では仲間の静止を振り切って勝手にボスに乗り込んだりするし、自分の分身という感じは全く無く、黙って勝手に行動する迷惑なやつなんだ。ホウレンソウは大事だよ？

それから、キャラクターの精神的な成長・・・？
まあ幼稚園児が母親に怒られてしおらしくなる程度の変化はあったか。成長かなぁ？
人間の精神的な成長は、迷いとか後悔を前提としてそれを乗り越える段階を通過することで成長が感じられると思っているのだけど、本作のキャラはそもそも迷いとかあんまりなさそう（そういう演出だろう）だから、成長というよりは例えば破滅的願望が成就していくとかのステージが進んでいく感じを成長と錯覚しているだけなんじゃないかと感じる。
何を言ってるかわからないと思うけど、本編のストーリーもこういうふわとした抽象文が大半ですよ、というところ。
ストーリーや構成を重視する人には、全くオススメできません。

Se tem um jogo que que exala carisma e melancolia ao mesmo tempo é esse jogo, infelizmente não tem uma tradução em PT-BR oficial, mas se você tem uma boa noção de inglês é bem tranquilo entender a história, que é simplesmente fenomenal. O grande forte desse jogo é definitivamente a humanização dos personagens, as atitudes que eles tomam e o desenvolvimento deles, é um metroidvania com uma narrativa de outro mundo, coisa que não vejo a cada esquina por aí, se não se convenceu ainda vou te dizer alguns elementos do jogo sem dar grandes spoilers, tem um pessoal que tem um fanatismo religioso aí que regula absolutamente tudo, até quem pode ou não trabalhar, e você não tem licença pra trabalhar como mecânica mas você faz mesmo assim porque gosta de ajudar os outros, tudo gira em torno de um controle social bem estabelecido, culpa e responsabilidade por parte de decisões que sua personagem e outros amigos seus tomam, nem tudo é preto no branco, não tem mocinho e vilão certo, é só um monte de gente seguindo seus ídolos ou fazendo o que bem entende apesar dos riscos.

Vale mencionar que Iconoclasts é um jogo feito majoritariamente por uma ÚNICA pessoa, o que fez com que demorasse uns 7 anos pra ser feito, eu fico meio triste por saber que, apesar da repercussão geral do jogo ter sido positiva, não ter feito um grande sucesso, pois ele merecia sim ser uma referência no gênero de metroidvania, a qualidade do jogo é impecável, a jogabilidade é fluída e fácil de entender sem contar que esse jogo é um charme, o cara que fez esse jogo é brabo demais, investiu 7 anos da vida dele nesse jogo e entregou uma das melhores experiências que já tive com metroidvanias, merecia mais reconhecimento.

[h1] 主人公がキュート、ボス戦はとにかく秀逸、ビジュアルの出来も申し分ないが…… [/h1]
まず、メガドラ風16bitのドットビジュアルと、そのアニメーションの豊富さを賞賛したい。
ディテールの端々から、作者のただ事ではないドット愛がうかがえるが、ゲーム性においても同じく非凡な出来を見せてくれる。
とりわけボス戦のつくりは出色の出来である。試行を重ねればノーダメで突破できる設計でありつつ、演出もひたすら冴え渡るため、プレイヤーの記憶にはいずれかのボス戦が確実に刻まれるであろう。
また、アクションゲームにおけるボス戦はタイマンが通例だが、このゲームでは仲間と共闘するボス戦が数多く見られる。
仲間の援護を経ての自キャラの攻勢、自分の行動を引き継いだ仲間による一撃など、ユニークなひねりが要所で設けられ、効果的に機能していた。
これらによる画面のにぎやかさとゲーム的盛り上がりが、プレイヤーにすさまじく強烈な印象を残すのだ。
マザー戦では味方３キャラとボスが入り乱れ死闘を繰り広げる、まさにこのゲームの華といっても過言ではない（「あたしの大地の一撃を喰らいな！」）。

しかしながら道中、エリアを突き進むパートにはあまり楽しさを見出だせなかった。

Religions aren't always a theocratic government bent on punnishing the wicked, but where the similarity resides is in the culture, the role we play, the storys we tell ourselves about the play by play of our lives. Our motives and how it determines our motives, and the legitimacy or maybe lack of legitimacy those stories and motives have on reality. 

There's a silent sitori (Zen Bhudist term. Look it up), that's found in this game, and it lingers with you for months after completing it. And it just... becomes a part of you.

Despite its flaws, Iconoclasts was just good enough to be above C-tier. If you want a true Metroidvania, I found myself pretty satisfied with this title. A lot of the bosses, however, featured really annoying and convoluted gimmicks that would only be used once, and when they were, they were either explained poorly (the Inti fight) or presented with no time to react (the Inti fight, again). Many of the characters were written very well, and others not so much; Chrome was one of my highlights, and Elro was one of the most bothersome lore characters I've ever seen. As I said, just above mid.

In the start, it felt extremely promising, the characters and setting were charming, and I had a lotta hope that it'll continue being so engaging as it goes on and the challenges becomes more complex. But more often than not, I'm finding that the complexity is created through tedious backtracking and confusing level design. Yeah yeah, backtracking is normal in Metroidvanias, but you gotta make the movement become more fun at some point, but we can't dash, we can't double-jump, all we can do is walk, jump, and hang from platforms, and it just all feels kinda clumsy and incomplete. The combat is also nothing to write home about, you have one clumsy melee weapon and two guns (of which only one is really practical for combat). The "Tweaks" you can equip don't give you any additional flexibility or so, they mostly make exploration a tad more convenient.

I was honestly into the underlying story and the worldbuilding, but the gameplay to me feels like a drag. It's honestly just inches away from a good game, though, so writing this review stings. I do respect what the developer went for and I hope I can be more positive about their next project.

[h1]Wrenching[/h1]
TL;DR: A weird, middling little action game that doesn’t do enough to stand out in a crowded genre.[hr][/hr]
Occasionally I buy a game based on whim and vibes, instead of my usual routine of relying on trusted reviewers to help filter out most of the chaff. [i]Iconoclasts[/i] was one such purchase, and while I enjoyed it well enough, I didn’t find it terribly compelling. It is a science fiction story-driven game search-action (or at least that’s the genre it most closely hews to) title that never quite manages to find its footing.

You play as Robin, an underground mechanic on a planet dominated by a dystopian religion / government known as the One Concern. This seemingly almighty cult strictly guards access to technology and strives to confine the thoughts of the populace similar to The Party in George Orwell’s [i]1984[/i], punishing deviations with “divine” eradication. The story that unfolds over the course of the game has you digging into the planet’s history, both literally and metaphorically, and revealing the true intentions at the heart of the One Concern’s operations. It’s a compelling setup, but the game’s tone is a bizarre mixture of cutesy slapstick humor with body- and cosmic-horror all set in an authoritarian hellscape. That blend may be up somebody’s alley, but for my tastes it never found the right balance, and wound up feeling constant tonal whiplash.

The gameplay was similarly dissonant, vacillating between fairly standard side-scrolling action-platforming exploration (with the requisite puzzles and secrets) and boss fights that tended to rely on teasing out gimmicks rather than mastery of the combat mechanics. It was mostly enjoyable, but nothing really felt clever enough to make a lasting impression. There were a few stand-out boss encounters where I was impressed based on enemy design, but more often I found myself replaying early phases that I’d grown bored of as I tried to learn a gimmick later in the fight. It never got so frustrating that I wanted to quit, but neither was it compelling.

In conclusion, Iconoclasts is a land of contrasts. I liked it well enough to finish it, but it felt too internally inconsistent to really hit with me, and I don’t feel compelled to recommend it. It is impressive as a largely solo-developer project, but it just didn’t feel fully compatible with my tastes.

Mechanically, this is a great 2D Metroidvania! Everything technical and aesthetic about it is top notch, it's got great sprite work and sound design, it feels phenomenal to play, and it's very creative with some really unique puzzles and plenty of secrets that are worth searching for.

The writing, on the other hand, is more mixed for me. The overall concept is great and there are some scenes that are incredibly well done. The world is alive and some of the twists hit pretty hard. There are also, however, just as many scenes where the dialogue is a little stilted and awkward, and it's not entirely clear what they're trying to get across. 

I still heavily recommend playing Iconoclasts, since the gameplay is what matters in this genre and it does all of that extremely well. I also do think the writing is better than average, the lackluster parts only stand out to me because I feel like this game had the pieces in place to tell a truly phenomenal story. While it didn't live up to that potential, it's still commendable that it had such a promising world and cast in the first place and I wouldn't be surprised if some of these characters and scenes truly resonate with a player with different tastes than myself.

If you're into Metroidvanias or 2D platformers at all, this is well worth full price.

说真的，在玩《叛逆机械师》之前，我也担心过这类游戏会不会又是个“玩法扎实、剧情凑数”的模板作品。但十多个小时流程下来，我彻底被折服了——它居然在有限的篇幅里，把一群角色的故事讲得如此鲜活、动人。

这游戏的灵魂，绝对是它笔下的人物。主角罗宾一句台词没有，却靠着行动成为我心中那朵永远灿烂的“小葵花”，她的善良与坚韧贯穿始终。而她的伙伴们更是各有各的精彩：冲动的米娜其实重情重义，看似软弱的哥哥埃尔罗有着最真实的恐惧与关爱，而那位骄傲的圣子罗伊尔，其悲剧性结局更是让无数玩家争论不休，后劲十足。就连反派也毫不脸谱化，特工“黑”的悲情与将军克罗姆的复杂谋算，都让这个世界显得真实而深刻。不得不说，这种全员“有血有肉”的塑造功力，在同类游戏中实属罕见。

除了顶尖的叙事，游戏本身的素质也相当扎实。它用一把扳手和三把枪，构建出了充满巧思的解谜与战斗，那些机制独特的BOSS战打得人拍案叫绝（或者拍桌猛骂，隐藏boss圣母边上两个狗头子突出一个你打你的我打我的）。精美的像素画面和应景的音乐，更是让这场冒险的视听体验全程在线，整体对新手非常友好，让你能轻松沉浸到故事中去。

独立开发者Joakim Sandberg用了七年时间打磨的《叛逆机械师》是一部将叙事与玩法精巧融合的杰作。它或许没有追求极致的难度或深不见底的探索，但却用心讲述了一个关于反抗、成长与代价的精彩故事，并留下了一群让你久久难忘的角色。如果你也厌倦了“哑巴主角”和工具人配角，那么罗宾的这场叛逆之旅，绝对值得你亲自体验。

全成就Tips：类银常见的能力锁全收集+隐藏boss+二周目要素，难度虽有三档但不限制休闲还是普通还是困难通关，一周目休闲全收集，二周目NG+带着双钢芯、二段跳和一周目的鲜活记忆，25h左右即可全成就。

 GAMEPLAY

Até a parte da neve o jogo já deixa claro que ele é metroidvania-lite: não é tão travado em backtracking, mas tem aquela sensação de “vou abrindo caminho na marra”.
A Robin, com a pistola e a chave inglesa, dá um gameplay que mistura plataforma rápida com quebra-cabeça na marra. Não é nada complexo demais, mas é satisfatório.
As mecânicas de girar parafusos, carregar energia e ativar mecanismos fazem o jogo parecer bem físico, tá ligado? Tu sente que tá mexendo no mundo.

 ESTÉTICA

O jogo é pixel art 2D, mas não é aquele pixel genérico. Tem cor, tem movimento, tem uma vibe meio “mundo quebrado mas bonito”.
As animações são suaves, e os cenários antes da neve já mostram que o jogo manda bem em criar ambientes que te dão curiosidade real de continuar andando.
A trilha sonora é boa de verdade, tu sente ela te jogando pra frente, mas sem ser barulhera.

 PERSONAGENS E ATMOSFERA

Sem spoiler: tu vai conhecendo alguns personagens que parecem “normais”, mas tu sente que tá rolando algo muito maior por trás.
O jogo tem um tom meio pesado escondido num visual fofinho. Tu percebe que cada área tem uma história própria, e até a parte da neve tu já fica meio “mano, tem algo errado nesse mundinho”.

 RITMO

Até chegar na neve, o jogo te dá um ritmo bem equilibrado:

um pouco de puzzle, um pouco de combate, um pouco de narrativa, e áreas que não te cansam.

É o tipo de jogo que tu joga sem travar, sem precisar ficar lendo tutorial toda hora.

 RESUMO

Iconoclasts até a parte da neve é:

Divertido de jogar, bem animado, misterioso na medida, e com uma vibe forte de “isso aqui vai ficar mais doido ainda”.
